title: Qudian Inc. Announces Name and Ticker Change
summary: XIAMEN, China , Dec. 11, 2025 /PRNewswire/ -- Qudian Inc. (" Qudian " or "the Company" or "We") (NYSE: QD), a consumer-oriented technology company in China , today announced the change of its name to " High Templar Tech Limited " and its ticker symbol to "HTT".
body_text: XIAMEN, China , Dec. 11, 2025 /PRNewswire/ -- Qudian Inc. ("Qudian" or "the Company" or "We") (NYSE: QD), a consumer-oriented technology company in China, today announced the change of its name to "High Templar Tech Limited" and its ticker symbol to "HTT". As previously announced by the Company on November 12, 2025, its board of directors (the "Board") resolved to (i) change the Company's name to "High Templar Tech Limited" (the "Name Change"), subject to shareholders' approval to be obtained at an extraordinary general meeting of shareholders (the "EGM"), and (ii) change the ticker symbol to "HTT". At the EGM held on December 10, 2025, the Company's shareholders approved the Name Change by a special resolution. The Company's American Depositary Shares ("ADSs"), each representing one Class A ordinary shares, par value of US$0.0001 per share, of the Company, are currently listed on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol "QD". The Company's ADSs are expected to begin trading under the Company's new name, "High Templar Tech Limited", and its new ticker symbol, "HTT", effective at the opening of trading on December 22, 2025. About Qudian Inc. Qudian Inc. (to be renamed as High Templar Tech Limited) (NYSE: QD) (to be changed to HTT) is a consumer-oriented technology company. Qudian is exploring innovative business opportunities to satisfy consumers' demand by leveraging its technology capabilities. For more information, please visit http://ir.qudian.com . For investor and media inquiries, please contact: In China: Qudian Inc. Tel: +86-592-596-8208 E-mail: ir@qudian.com View original content: https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/qudian-inc-announces-name-and-ticker-change-302638721.html SOURCE Qudian Inc.

title: Why Agentic AI Matters More in 2026
summary: 2026 will be the year enterprises bring intelligence into the heart of the employee experience platform. They will combine workplace technology, data, and agentic AI to remove friction and help employees move through their day with more clarity.
body_text: Several forces are making agentic AI a central theme for 2026 workplace strategy: 1. The volume of digital tasks keeps growing Employees interact with dozens of tools every day. Booking spaces, checking schedules, reading updates, submitting requests, finding people, searching for information, confirming events. These small tasks create constant switching and slow the workday. Agentic AI can reduce these micro-frictions by handling routine requests, routing issues, prompting next steps, and supporting employees in context. 2. Hybrid work demands faster, clearer decision making Hybrid work has stabilized, but employee patterns still shift week to week. People want clear information about onsite days, events, space availability, and resources. Agentic AI can answer these questions in seconds and take care of the follow-up. 3. Leaders want unified workplace journeys The strongest workplace experience platforms in 2026 will not be a collection of widgets. They will be a single app supported by intelligent agents behind the scenes. This combination helps employees stay informed, navigate the workplace, get support, and complete tasks without switching between ten different tools. 4. Enterprise systems are now ready for agentic capabilities Large vendors across ITSM, productivity, and identity are embedding agentic functions. APIs are improving. Workflows are easier to orchestrate. AI models are more capable. The environment is ideal for EX platforms to take advantage of this shift. What Agentic AI Does Inside a Workplace App Agentic AI inside an Employee Experience (EX) platform is not theoretical. It performs very practical, high frequency tasks that influence how the workplace feels. Examples include: Helping employees find information quickly Sending contextual reminders when someone arrives onsite Routing service requests to the right team Recommending events or onsite resources Helping employees plan their day and navigate the workplace Clearing simple issues before they reach support teams Offering guidance during busy periods or high traffic days Surfacing insights to leaders about engagement patterns Completing small tasks across systems without manual steps This is how the workplace app becomes more of a guide than a menu of links. How CXAI Uses Agentic AI To Improve The Workday CXAI is building agentic capabilities that support daily workplace journeys in ways employees feel immediately. 1. Clear, helpful support Employees no longer need to guess which team to contact. AI routes requests to the right group and resolves simple issues on the spot. 2. Insight-driven experiences Agents identify patterns in space usage, communication engagement, and event interest. Leaders get cleaner signals and can adjust programs quickly. 3. Smoother onsite days When an employee arrives on campus, agentic AI can surface the information they need for that day. Parking details, events, booked rooms, relevant updates, people nearby, and more. 4. Less noise Employees receive only what is relevant. Agents help filter workplace updates so communication feels supportive, not overwhelming. 5. Proactive, not reactive CXAI’s roadmap includes agents that anticipate needs, offer next best actions, and guide employees through common flows like onboarding, guest hosting, and navigating new buildings. What Leaders Should Consider When Planning for 2026 Here are questions guiding many Workplace leaders as they explore agentic AI: Where are the biggest friction points for employees today Look at moments that create delays, confusion, or unnecessary switching. These often reveal the best opportunities for AI agents. How many tools are employees expected to use Organizations with five or more tools supporting daily workplace tasks see the fastest EX gains when shifting to a unified app with AI support. What is the change management plan Agentic AI is most effective when employees understand its purpose and when leaders communicate clearly how it supports real work. What data do we want to unlock AI agents are most powerful when they can access meaningful signals. Space usage, engagement, event behavior, request patterns, and campus flows are great starting points. How do we measure success Adoption, reduced/accessible support tickets, faster employee resolution times, stronger onsite engagement, and improved satisfaction scores are all common KPIs. What This Means for Workplace Experience Teams Agentic AI will not replace the workplace experience team. It will help teams scale. It becomes another way to provide support, guide employees, personalize communication, and sharpen insight across HR, IT, Real Estate, and Workplace Experience groups. Leaders get more visibility into what employees need. Employees get a smoother, more intuitive journey. The workplace app becomes a partner rather than a set of links. Conclusion: 2026 Will Be a Defining Year 2026 will be the year enterprises bring intelligence into the heart of the employee experience platform. They will combine workplace technology, data, and agentic AI to remove friction and help employees move through their day with more clarity. CXAI is preparing for this shift today. The combination of a single workplace app and intelligent AI support is a powerful step toward making workplace experience feel connected, adaptive, and human. Enterprises that invest now will see stronger adoption, improved engagement, and better outcomes in 2026. Learn more about Agentic AI and the CXAI workplace & employee experience app.

Why AI Platforms Avoid Citing Fintech Companies (And Why Traditional SEO Can't Fix It)
summary: AI platforms cite banks and financial media over fintechs due to YMYL standards. Learn why traditional SEO can't build the authority signals AI requires.
body_text: In a Nutshell AI platforms heavily favor established publishers over fintechs when YMYL standards require institutional authority 82% of AI citations come from earned media, specifically journalism and established outlets with years of press coverage Traditional SEO can't build the authority signals (credentialed authors, regulatory citations, earned media) AI platforms require for financial content Table of Contents Why AI Platforms Favor Financial Publishers Over Fintech Companies The Three-Tier Authority Hierarchy That Determines Citations Why YMYL Compliance Requires Specialized Fintech AI Expertise Frequently Asked Questions Why AI Platforms Favor Financial Publishers Over Fintech Companies Your fintech company publishes excellent content about investment strategies, retirement planning, or financial decision-making. It ranks decently on Google. But when prospects ask ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, or Claude for financial advice, AI platforms predominantly cite traditional banks and financial media. This isn't hypothetical. 66% of Americans using generative AI have already used it for financial tasks, and with 800 million people using ChatGPT weekly, AI platforms have become where prospects start their financial research. This pattern is systematic, not random. Google's YMYL (Your Money or Your Life) framework gives even more weight to E-E-A-T , which stands for Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness, and Trustworthiness, for topics affecting financial stability. AI platforms show similar citation patterns, heavily favoring established sources with proven authority signals. Muck Rack, a media intelligence platform, reports that 82% of AI citations come from earned media , specifically journalism and established outlets with years of press coverage. The result is predictable: fintechs without extensive press history and institutional recognition face steep visibility disadvantages. Content quality alone doesn't overcome the authority gap. Building YMYL-compliant authority requires earned media relationships, credentialed authors, and regulatory alignment. This filtering operates from a clear three-tier hierarchy that determines which financial sources AI platforms trust. This doesn't mean fintechs are permanently excluded. Fintechs with strong authority signals, earned media presence, and proper technical optimization can achieve significant AI visibility. But it requires specialized expertise that most traditional SEO agencies lack, and the timeline is measured in years, not months. The Three-Tier Authority Hierarchy That Determines Citations AI platforms show a rigid hierarchy for financial content that structurally advantages established institutions over fintechs. Tier Who's In This Tier Authority Signals Citation Priority Tier 1 Government bodies, regulators, central banks Legal authority, regulatory frameworks, policy-setting power Cited first for regulatory and compliance questions Tier 2 Established financial media (NerdWallet, Investopedia) Years of press coverage, extensive backlinks from Tier 1, institutional recognition Dominates consumer-facing financial advice and product comparisons Tier 3 Fintechs and newer financial brands Limited press history, fewer regulatory citations, developing institutional relationships Rarely cited in AI responses despite content quality For example, a fintech offering superior robo-advisor technology but without Wall Street Journal features, SEC citations, or regulatory press coverage faces an uphill climb in AI visibility. An established bank's basic explainer, by contrast, carries the weight of years of earned authority and institutional recognition. The U.S. Treasury, the federal department managing national finances, publishes documents on AI in financial services that shape policy discussions. The Financial Stability Board, an international body coordinating financial regulation, and the Bank of England, the UK's central bank, provide frameworks and regulatory guidance that shape how risk is understood across the industry. When prospects research "how to evaluate investment platforms," AI cites regulatory guidance first. Established financial media like NerdWallet, a personal finance platform, and Investopedia, a financial education site, dominate Tier 2 citations because of years of press coverage and extensive backlink profiles from Tier 1 sources. December 2025 analysis identifies these as the most frequently cited finance sources in AI platforms. Your prospects see these brands during their AI-powered research phase, forming opinions before they reach your site. Why YMYL Compliance Requires Specialized Fintech AI Expertise Traditional SEO focuses on keywords and backlinks. But for financial content, the requirements go far deeper. Your SEO agency optimizes for Google's algorithm. But AI platform optimization for financial content requires understanding YMYL compliance standards that affect citation decisions, how to build earned media profiles AI platforms trust, platform-specific authority signals across ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, and Claude, and the multi-year timeline for establishing financial content authority. What AI Platforms Actually Evaluate for Financial Content AI platforms prioritize named authors with verifiable financial credentials like CFP, CFA, or advisory licenses. They look for citations from Tier 1 sources including government agencies, regulators, and academic institutions. They evaluate earned media in recognized financial publications, not just backlinks. Academic research confirms that financial literacy significantly increases advice-seeking behavior, and AI platforms reflect this by prioritizing credentialed voices. Domain age, consistent publishing history, transparent editorial standards, and regulatory compliance all signal trustworthiness over time. These authority signals require 18-24 months of consistent publishing with credentialed authors, earned media development, and Tier 1 citations to establish. The Stakes Are Rising Fast The competitive landscape is intensifying as fintech growth accelerates and AI platforms become the primary research channel for financial decisions. By the Numbers: McKinsey & Company, a global consulting firm, projects fintech revenues growing at 15% annually compared to 6% for traditional banking , more than twice as fast, reaching over $400 billion by 2028. In a market growing this explosively, early-mover advantage in AI visibility compounds quickly. The specialization gap is fundamental. Generic SEO tactics focus on quick wins: keyword optimization, technical fixes, backlink building. YMYL authority requires specialized expertise in earned media development and credentialed content strategies that traditional SEO agencies don't typically offer. Key Insight: The fintechs building proper authority signals now will capture citations as AI search grows and shapes financial services competition. Traditional SEO tactics optimize for today's Google rankings while prospects increasingly research financial solutions through AI platforms that consistently sideline companies lacking institutional credibility. This creates a clear fork in the road for fintech leadership. The Strategic Choice As AI reshapes how prospects evaluate financial solutions, fintechs face a clear decision. You can continue investing in traditional SEO that improves Google rankings but leaves you largely invisible during the AI-powered research phase. Or you can build YMYL-compliant AI authority through specialized AI search for fintech , expertise in earned media, credentialed authors, and regulatory alignment. The window for action is narrowing. Prospects are already using ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, and Claude to research investment platforms, retirement planning tools, and financial decision-making frameworks. They're forming opinions based on sources AI platforms trust. Without proper authority signals, your excellent content rarely enters that conversation. The bottom line: AI platforms heavily favor established publishers over fintechs for YMYL content, requiring institutional authority signals that traditional SEO can't build. The 82% of AI citations favoring earned media reflect years of press coverage and credentialed authorship that generic SEO agencies can't create. Building YMYL authority takes 18-24 months. The fintechs that start now own the citations when prospects ask AI platforms for financial advice. The question is whether your fintech will be visible during that research phase, or whether prospects will form opinions based on competitors and established financial media alone. title: UK: TotalEnergies merges its Upstream business with NEO NEXT, creating the largest independent oil and gas producer in the UK
summary: TotalEnergies will merge its UK Upstream business with NEO NEXT, positioning the new NEO NEXT+ as the largest independent oil and gas producer in the UK. TotalEnergies will have a 47.5% shareholding interest in the broadened NEO NEXT+. The new shareholding structure, asset portfolio and size of NEO NEXT+ will foster synergies and strong cash […]
body_text: TotalEnergies will merge its UK Upstream business with NEO NEXT, positioning the new NEO NEXT+ as the largest independent oil and gas producer in the UK. TotalEnergies will have a 47.5% shareholding interest in the broadened NEO NEXT+. The new shareholding structure, asset portfolio and size of NEO NEXT+ will foster synergies and strong cash flow, while contributing to energy supply for the UK. Paris, December 8, 2025 – TotalEnergies has signed an agreement with NEO NEXT Energy Limited (NEO NEXT) under which TotalEnergies will merge its Upstream business with NEO NEXT and become the leading shareholder in the expanded NEO NEXT, which will be renamed NEO NEXT+, with a 47.5% ownership. After completion of the transaction, NEO NEXT+ will: be jointly owned by TotalEnergies (47.5%), HitecVision (28.875%) and Repsol UK (23.625%) and encompass a large and diverse asset portfolio including notably NEO Energy's and Repsol UK's interests in the Elgin/Franklin complex and the Penguins, Mariner, Shearwater and Culzean fields, enriched by TotalEnergies' UK Upstream assets, notably including its interests in the Elgin/Franklin complex and the Alwyn North, Dunbar and Culzean fields. With TotalEnergies as its leading shareholder, NEO NEXT+ will become the largest independent oil and gas producer in the UK with a production over 250,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day in 2026, ideally positioned to maximize the value of its portfolio, deliver strong financial returns and ensure a long-term sustainable and resilient future for its oil & gas business. “This transaction demonstrates the long-lasting commitment of TotalEnergies towards the UK oil and gas sector and its energy security. As the new largest shareholder of NEO NEXT+, we are excited to bring along our recognized track record as a leading operator in the UK North Sea, where we have been present for more than 60 years. TotalEnergies' consistent focus on running low-cost and low-emissions operations will be instrumental in delivering material economies of scale within the new portfolio of NEO NEXT+, that will enhance the cash flow generation of the Company as soon as it is closed,” said Patrick Pouyanné, Chairman and CEO of TotalEnergies . Completion of the transaction is subject to customary conditions, including regulatory approvals and is expected during the first half of 2026. ***

title: Debug GitHub Actions in live CI environment with AI
summary: A comprehensive guide to debugging GitHub Actions CI failures by SSH-ing into the live runner environment. Covers Tailscale (zero-config) and Cloudflare Tunnel (SSH key) approaches with step-by-step setup instructions. Uses Cursor as the IDE and AI assistants for real-time debugging.
body_text: The Problem Debugging CI failures often devolves into a frustrating cycle: make a change, push, wait for the build, hit the next error, repeat. This happens because replicating the CI environment locally is difficult—or sometimes impossible when dealing with OAuth tokens, cloud IAM roles, or environment-specific configurations. This guide shows you how to break that cycle by SSH-ing directly into your live CI environment when a job fails. You'll get full IDE access (with AI coding assistants) and an interactive terminal to diagnose and fix issues in real-time. Supported IDEs This guide uses Cursor . Any VS Code fork may work but alternatives have not been tested. Prerequisites Remote-SSH extension installed in Cursor/VS Code A GitHub repository with Actions workflows For Tailscale method: A Tailscale account For SSH method: An SSH key pair and Cloudflare CLI Method 1: Tailscale (Recommended) Tailscale provides a zero-trust mesh VPN that eliminates SSH key management entirely. Authentication is handled through your identity provider, and devices on your tailnet can communicate directly without exposing ports to the public internet. Why Tailscale? No SSH keys to configure, rotate, or store in secrets. Keyless authentication via your identity provider. Ephemeral nodes auto-remove when the runner terminates. Setup Tailscale Create a Tailscale account Sign up at login.tailscale.com/start . This creates your personal tailnet—a private mesh network for your devices. Add your local machine to the tailnet Follow the Tailscale device setup guide to install Tailscale on your development machine. Verify it appears in your admin dashboard . Generate an ephemeral auth key Navigate to Settings → Personal Settings → Keys in the Tailscale admin console. Click Generate auth key with these options: Ephemeral : Enabled (auto-removes the device when disconnected) Reusable : Enabled (allows the same key for multiple runner registrations) Add the auth key to GitHub Secrets In your repository, go to Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions and create a new secret named TAILSCALE_AUTH_KEY_DEBUG with your generated auth key. Configure the Workflow Add this step to your workflow after the step that's failing. It connects the runner to your tailnet and keeps the job alive for debugging: - name : Setup Tailscale SSH if : ${{ failure() }} run : | # Write secret to temp file mkdir -p /tmp/secrets echo "${{ secrets.TAILSCALE_AUTH_KEY_DEBUG }}" > /tmp/secrets/tailscale_auth_key chmod 600 /tmp/secrets/tailscale_auth_key # Install Tailscale curl -fsSL https://tailscale.com/install.sh | sh # Start Tailscale with auth key and SSH enabled sudo tailscale up --auth-key=$(cat /tmp/secrets/tailscale_auth_key) --hostname=gha-debug-${GITHUB_RUN_ID} --ssh # Get connection info TAILSCALE_IP=$(tailscale ip -4) TAILSCALE_HOSTNAME="gha-debug-${GITHUB_RUN_ID}" echo "" echo "========================================" echo "SSH INTO RUNNER" echo "========================================" echo "ssh runner@$TAILSCALE_IP" echo "ssh runner@$TAILSCALE_HOSTNAME" echo "" echo "OPEN IN CURSOR:" echo "cursor --folder-uri \"vscode-remote://ssh-remote+runner%40$TAILSCALE_IP/home/runner/work/\"" echo "========================================" echo "" echo "(Keeping job alive; cancel the workflow when done debugging.)" tail -f /dev/null Connect from Cursor When the workflow fails, the step above logs a Cursor command. Copy and run it in your terminal: cursor --folder-uri "vscode-remote://ssh-remote+runner%40100.88.xx.xx/home/runner/work/" Cursor opens directly to the runner's workspace. You now have full IDE access with integrated terminal and AI assistance. Method 2: SSH with Cloudflare Tunnel If you can't use Tailscale, this method uses traditional SSH keys with Cloudflare Tunnel to expose the runner's SSH port without a public IP. Trade-offs This approach requires managing SSH keys and updating your local SSH config for each debug session. It's more complex but works in environments where Tailscale isn't an option. Setup SSH Keys Generate an SSH key pair (if needed) Check for existing keys with ls ~/.ssh . If you need a new key, generate one: ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "github-actions-debug" See the GitHub SSH key guide for details. Add the private key to GitHub Secrets Create a secret named SSH_PRIVATE_KEY_DEBUG containing your private key (the file without the .pub extension). Configure the Workflow Add these steps after the failing step. They configure SSH and create a Cloudflare tunnel: - name : Setup SSH private key if : ${{ failure() }} run : | mkdir -p ~/.ssh echo "${{ secrets.SSH_PRIVATE_KEY_DEBUG }}" > ~/.ssh/custom_key chmod 600 ~/.ssh/custom_key ssh-keygen -y -f ~/.ssh/custom_key > ~/.ssh/custom_key.pub chmod 644 ~/.ssh/custom_key.pub cat >> ~/.ssh/config << 'EOF' Host * IdentityFile ~/.ssh/custom_key AddKeysToAgent yes EOF chmod 600 ~/.ssh/config - name : Start SSH session with Cloudflare Tunnel if : ${{ failure() }} uses : valeriangalliat/action-sshd-cloudflared@v1 Connect from Cursor Clear any cached host keys ssh-keygen -R action-sshd-cloudflared Configure the SSH proxy Add a host entry to ~/.ssh/config using the hostname from the action output: Host cf-gha HostName action-sshd-cloudflared User runner ProxyCommand cloudflared access tcp --hostname <hostname-from-action-output> StrictHostKeyChecking accept-new Replace <hostname-from-action-output> with the Cloudflare hostname (e.g., facilities-canvas-frequency-reasonable.trycloudflare.com ). Open Cursor cursor --folder-uri "vscode-remote://ssh-remote+cf-gha/home/runner/work/" Production Considerations Finding Runner Logs When debugging with AI assistants, you'll often want to feed them the full job logs. WarpBuild runners store logs at: Image Log Location Ubuntu x86-64 /runner/_diag/*.log Ubuntu ARM64 24.04 /runner/_diag/*.log Windows x86-64 C:\warpbuilds\runner\_diag\*.log macOS ARM64 /Users/runner/.warpbuild/github-runner/runner-app-new/_diag/*.log Timeout and Notifications Keeping a runner alive indefinitely burns CI minutes. Add a timeout and optional Slack notification for visibility: - name : Notify on failure if : ${{ failure() }} uses : rtCamp/action-slack-notify@v2 env : SLACK_WEBHOOK : ${{ secrets.SLACK_WEBHOOK }} - name : Setup debug session if : ${{ failure() }} timeout-minutes : 30 # Auto-terminate after 30 minutes run : | # ... Tailscale or SSH setup from above Cost awareness GitHub Actions has a default job timeout of 6 hours. Without an explicit timeout-minutes , a forgotten debug session will continue burning minutes until it hits that limit. See rtCamp/action-slack-notify for notification configuration and GitHub's timeout documentation for step timeout syntax. title: Scholarship Essay Tips and Strategies for Winning Scholarships
summary: Scholarship Essay Tips and Strategies for Winning Scholarships Scholarship essays play a major role in how committees evaluate applicants. Good grades and test scores can help, but the essay is whe...
body_text: Scholarship Essay Tips and Strategies for Winning Scholarships Scholarship essays play a major role in how committees evaluate applicants. Good grades and test scores can help, but the essay is where reviewers learn who you are, what you value, and why you deserve financial support. A well-written essay can set you apart, even in a competitive applicant pool. This guide explains practical scholarship essay tips, strategies that help you stand out, and common mistakes to avoid. Students and parents can use these insights to approach the scholarship process with clarity and confidence. Why Scholarship Essays Matter Many scholarships attract students with strong transcripts, similar GPAs, and impressive extracurriculars. The essay gives committees something the rest of the application cannot: your voice. It helps them understand your personality, your motivations, and the experiences that shaped you. A strong scholarship essay can help you: Stand out in competitive pools Communicate academic or career goals Highlight meaningful experiences Demonstrate leadership and initiative Explain how financial support will help you reach your goals If you want to understand the broader admissions landscape as you plan your scholarship applications, you can explore Acely’s guide to college acceptance rates for 2026 . Understanding how colleges evaluate applicants can help you write an essay that shows your direction and strengths. Understand the Prompt Before You Start Writing Every strong scholarship essay begins with a clear understanding of the prompt. Scholarship committees design questions to learn something specific about you, so answering the prompt fully is important. Common Scholarship Essay Prompt Types Personal story or defining experience Academic or career goals Leadership or problem-solving Community involvement Overcoming a challenge Why you deserve the scholarship Before you start writing, ask yourself: What does this prompt want to learn about me Which experience best answers the question What message should the reader remember If you are applying to selective schools like Northeastern , understanding what they value can help you shape your narrative. Scholarship Essay Tips That Help You Stand Out The strategies below help your writing feel clear, confident, and personal. Start With a Clear and Engaging Opening Your introduction should make the reader want to continue. A simple reflection, moment, or story can draw the reader in without feeling dramatic or exaggerated. Be Honest and Specific Strong essays use real experiences and concrete details. Avoid broad statements that could apply to anyone. Choose examples that reflect who you are. Instead of saying, “I enjoy helping others,” try: “I volunteer each week with a second grade reading group where I help students build confidence through short stories and reading games.” Focus on Growth and Reflection Committees want to understand what you learned from your experiences. Growth can come from challenges, community involvement, leadership roles, or academic work. Connect Your Story to Your Future Plans Scholarships support students who have a clear direction. You do not need a perfect plan, but you should show how the scholarship will help you reach your goals. Keep Your Writing Clear and Organized Short paragraphs, simple transitions, and direct language make your essay easy to read. Clarity always matters more than complexity. Common Mistakes to Avoid These common issues weaken otherwise strong essays. Writing What You Think They Want to Hear Committees value authenticity. Use your natural voice. Turning the Essay Into a Resume Choose one or two meaningful experiences and explore them deeply. A list of achievements is not a story. Focusing Only on the Challenge If you write about a challenge, center your growth, not only the difficulty. Ignoring the Word Limit Stay within the required length. It shows discipline and respect for the reader. A Simple Structure You Can Use for Any Scholarship Essay A clear structure helps your ideas flow naturally and makes your writing more impactful. Introduction Short hook Clear connection to the prompt Body Paragraphs Describe your experience Explain why it matters Show what you learned Connect it to your goals Conclusion Reinforce your main message Show how the scholarship supports your next steps How to Edit and Improve Your Essay Editing is where your essay becomes stronger and more focused. Read the Essay Out Loud This helps you catch unclear or awkward sentences. Remove Unnecessary Words Concise writing is more powerful and easier to understand. Ask Someone You Trust for Feedback A teacher or counselor can help you refine your ideas and strengthen your message. Make Sure You Fully Answer the Prompt Many essays lose impact because they miss part of the question. Always read the prompt again before submitting. Next Steps as You Prepare Your Scholarship Essays Scholarship essays take time and revision, but students who plan ahead and write with honesty tend to submit stronger applications. Focus on prompts that let you highlight your strengths, be specific about your experiences, and connect your story to your goals. If you want to understand how colleges evaluate academic readiness, you can explore this helpful breakdown of score trends at top universities . Thoughtful planning and clear storytelling can help your essay stand out in any scholarship pool.

title: Sprott Focus Trust, Inc. (Nasdaq-FUND) Declares Fourth Quarter Common Stock Distribution of $0.1911 Per Share
summary: Sprott is a global investment manager specializing in precious metals and real assets investing.
body_text: TORONTO, Dec. 02, 2025 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Sprott Focus Trust, Inc. (Nasdaq-FUND) (the “Fund” or “FUND”) has declared a quarterly distribution of $0.1911 per share on its Common Stock. The distribution, optionally payable in additional shares of Common Stock or in cash by specific stockholder election, is to be paid on December 29, 2025 to stockholders of record at the close of business on December 12, 2025 (ex-dividend on December 12, 2025). The price of shares issued for reinvestment will be determined on December 19, 2025. The Fund currently has adopted a Distribution Policy of paying quarterly distributions on its Common Stock. Distributions are being made at the annual rate of 6% of the rolling average of the prior four calendar quarter-end net asset values (“NAVs”), with the fourth quarter distribution being the greater of 1.50% of the rolling average or the minimum distribution required by IRS regulations. The policy, including the annual rate, is subject to change at the discretion of the Fund’s Board of Directors.
